summary: Tsugunari Kubo (1936–2019) was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo and Rissho University. He served as president of Reiyukai and of the International Institute for Buddhist Studies, and lectured at Rissho University.

Tsui Lan Liza Cheung is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned her PhD at the University of Hong Kong (attested 2013). She studied under doctoral supervisor K. L. Dhammajoti and teacher Toshiichi Endo.

Tsukasa Mizushima (b. 1952) is an Indologist and historian who earned his degrees, including a doctorate, from the University of Tokyo. He held posts at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies and was an emeritus professor at the University of Tokyo.

Tsultrim Allione (b. 1947) works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She completed a master's at Antioch University and studied with traditional teachers including Chögyam Trungpa, the 16th Karmapa, and Namkhai Norbu. She founded Tara Mandala in 1993.

Tsultrim Gyatso is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He served as a senior instructor at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies and as Abbot of Drepung Gomang Dratsang (attested 1987).

Tsultrim Kelsang (b. 1939) is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar. He held teaching posts at Otani University, including lecturer (attested 1984) and professor (attested 1999–2002), and was a visiting researcher at Ryukoku University in 2015.

Tsuneki Nishiwaki (b. 1943) is a scholar of philosophy, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. After studying at Tokyo University of Education (1963–1971), he held posts at Doshisha University (~1978–1993) and served as a professor at Kyoto University (~1993–2007).

Tsuruji Sahoda (1899–1986) was an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied at Kyoto University from ~1920 to 1926. He subsequently held posts at Ritsumeikan University (~1928–1951) and Osaka University (~1951–1963).
Tsutomu Hatai (1923–2018) worked in Indology and other fields. Attested in 1987, he succeeded Hiroshi Maruyama and served as president of the Ayurveda Research Society.
Tsutomu Horio (b. 1949) is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies who studied under Keiji Nishitani. He served as a professor at Otani University (attested 1990).

Tsutomu Kubo (1883–1972) was a philosophy scholar who studied under Raphael von Koeber at the University of Tokyo and earned a doctorate from Tohoku University. He taught at Tohoku University (1929–1946) and Toyo University (~1949–1954).

Tsutomu Yamaguchi (b. 1953) is a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies who studied at Hokkaido University. He held researcher positions at the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute, attested in 2015 and 2026.

Tsuyoshi Yokoyama works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He pursued doctoral studies at Kyoto University (attested 2015–2017) and served as a specially appointed researcher at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (attested 2017).

Tsyben Zhamtsarano (1880–1942) was a scholar in Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics. He studied at Saint Petersburg State University in 1902 and later headed the Mongolian Academy of Sciences.

Tu Weiming (b. 1940) specializes in philosophy, Sinology, and religious studies. He studied at Tunghai, Tokai, and Harvard universities. His career includes professorships at UC Berkeley, Harvard, and Peking University, and directing the Harvard-Yenching Institute (1996–2008).

Tubten Chokyi Dorje studied under Patrul Rinpoche, Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye, and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso. He taught Shenphen Nangwa, Khenpo Ngawang Pelzang, Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, Dodrupchen Rinpoche, and Rangjung Rigpe Dorje.
Tubten Gyeltsen Ozer was a scholar who studied under Patrul Rinpoche, Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, and Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye.

Tubten Nyendrak (1883–1959) was a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied under Shenphen Nangwa, Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye, and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso, and taught Botrul Dongak Tenpai Nyima and Dodrupchen Rinpoche.
Tubten Nyima studied under Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö and Dodrupchen Rinpoche.
Tubten Tsondru studied under Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, Dodrupchen Rinpoche, Khunu Lama Tenzin Gyaltsen, and Khenpo Gangshar. He taught Khenchen Palden Sherab Rinpoche and Ringu Tulku.
